title: Choose the input mode
scenario: Four requests land on your desk in the same hour. Each one has material that exists as an artefact — a photo, a document, a recording — and you have an AI assistant that accepts text, images, audio and documents.
task: Pick the request where handing over the artefact itself is clearly the right first move — and check why the others are weaker uses of the tool.

options.text: A planning meeting ends and you need the decisions, owners and dates from a photo of the whiteboard.
options.feedback: The whiteboard is the evidence: arrows, groupings and exact wording survive in the photo. Attach it, ask for a table, then check each line against the photo — artefact in, structure out.

options.text: You need to quote a precise clause from a contract you can open and copy from.
options.feedback: This one is text. Copy the clause exactly and paste it in; retyping or re-describing it would only add transcription risk.

options.text: You remember the gist of a phone call and want a summary for your notes.
options.feedback: There is no artefact to attach — the material is your memory. A summary of your memory is fine for personal notes, but nothing here is being verified.

options.text: You want a general explanation of how shipping insurance claims work.
options.feedback: No private artefact is involved — this is a question about a general process, so plain text (and maybe a web search) is the right shape.

hints: Ask two questions: does the material exist as a file, and does its layout or wording carry meaning that a retelling would lose?
The strongest use is the one where the model can read the source itself instead of your version of it.
explanation: Multimodal input pays off when fidelity matters and the source exists: a whiteboard photo keeps the structure that a retyped list destroys. When the material is already text you can copy, use text; when it is a general question, no attachment is needed; when it is your memory, accept that you are summarising a summary. Match the input to what the task actually needs to preserve.
